input: Set up a fish tank in the kids' room

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this means buying everything from scratch vs. setting up an already-owned tank changes the entire plan — one starts at a store, the other starts with assembly.
Tank size, equipment quality, and fish species all scale directly with budget; a $50 plan looks completely different from a $500 plan.
The age(s) of the kids affects safety considerations (e.g. childproofing, lid security), maintenance responsibility, and even what fish are appropriate.
Room size, available surfaces or furniture, and proximity to a water source affect what tank size is feasible and where it can realistically go.
Freshwater vs. saltwater, specific fish types, or a themed tank (tropical, planted, etc.) drive equipment choices, cost, and complexity of maintenance.
Whether the user wants to do this alone, with help, or involve the kids directly affects how tasks should be sequenced and described.
Knowing whether 'done' means water is cycling, fish are in the tank, or the kids are independently maintaining it sets the right endpoint for the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a fish tank in the kids' room
gold.taskDescription: Plan and execute the full setup of a fish tank placed in a child's bedroom, from choosing equipment to having fish living in it.

questions.title: Do you already own a tank and equipment?
questions.description: Establish whether this is a purchase-everything-from-scratch project or assembling and setting up gear that is already on hand.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this setup?
questions.description: Determine the spending limit to guide tank size, equipment tier, and fish species selection.

questions.title: How old are the kids who will have this tank?
questions.description: Age shapes safety requirements, how childproof the setup needs to be, and how much maintenance responsibility the kids can realistically take on.

questions.title: Where in the room is the tank going to sit?
questions.description: Identify whether a surface, stand, or furniture already exists for the tank, and how close it is to an electrical outlet and water source.

questions.title: What type of fish or tank style do you want?
questions.description: Understand whether the goal is a simple freshwater community tank, a planted aquascape, a saltwater reef, or a specific fish species, as this drives all equipment decisions.

questions.title: Will you be setting it up alone or with the kids?
questions.description: Knowing who is involved in the physical setup helps determine how tasks should be broken down, sequenced, and described in the plan.

questions.title: What does a successful finish line look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify whether 'done' means the tank is assembled and cycling, fish are swimming in it, or the kids are independently feeding and maintaining it.
